exchanges.analyst: None (scripted management discussion led by Chris Seibert)
exchanges.question: Not an analyst exchange: scripted Q2 results, FY2026 guidance and moderated management discussion (quarter breakdown, IEEPA refunds and tariffs, regional ag markets, construction, inventory, guidance changes, ag innovation, closing remarks) before analyst Q&A.
exchanges.answer: Q2 results and FY2026 outlook given (see metrics and guidance); $272 million IEEPA refund recovery lifted margins nearly 2.5 points; direct tariff exposure unchanged at ~$1.2 billion (~3% margin headwind), ~$900 million net of refunds. South America industry cut to down 15% from down 5% on Brazil; C&F sales guide raised to ~+20% and margin to 10%-12%; US/Canada C&F order book up more than 60% since November, over 80% of production slots filled. Baseline view that 2026 is the bottom of the ag cycle; new and used inventories much improved; back half revenue higher with Q4 above Q3. Returned $635 million to shareholders in the quarter; commitment to $20 billion of U.S. manufacturing investment over 10 years.

exchanges.question: With construction industry guided up 5% but Deere's sales growing much faster, is industry growth healthy and is Deere gaining a lot of share?
exchanges.answer: Last year's earthmoving underproduction, mostly in the front part of the year, gives a natural lift as production aligns with retail; industry up 5% in earthmoving plus road building strength; also some share gains over the past 12 months, particularly the last six or so after pricing adjustments at the end of last year.

exchanges.question: Break down the $272 million tariff refund by segment to understand baseline margins.
exchanges.answer: Tariff expense run rate unchanged at about $1.2 billion: about 45% C&F, about a third SAT, about 20% large ag; full-year impact about 3 points. The $272 million refund is about a point of full-year tailwind for equipment operations; about 50% went to C&F, about 30% to SAT, the remaining 20% to large ag.

exchanges.question: Since Deere has not priced for tariffs, what mitigation strategies are in place, what progress has been made over the last 12 months, and what is still to come?
exchanges.answer: Norwood: equipment operations price forecast about 1.5%-2%, matching general inflation ex tariffs of about 1.5%-2%, so tariffs are margin dilutive; no surcharges; mitigation via resourcing, reshoring, exemption submissions and USMCA compliance; full confidence tariffs will be largely countered over coming periods through cost measures. Beal: back half laps last year's tariff and inflation costs and last year's C&F and large ag incentives, so price-cost improves through the balance of the fiscal year. No quantified mitigation progress given.

exchanges.question: How should we frame downside risk to regional ag outlooks given the abnormal geopolitical environment, and are there past periods that serve as a reference for farmer behavior?
exchanges.answer: Beal: a couple of years into the downturn with very elevated fleet age for high horsepower tractors and combines; used inventory healthier, MY2022-2023 high horsepower tractors down like 45% from peak; fertilizer increases pressure margins, most acutely in Brazil; baseline remains recovery in 2027 with some replacement returning, pace dependent on policy, fundamentals and geopolitics. Seibert: regions differ; U.S. soybean and corn prices up like 20% since August with inputs secured, so this year may look a little better than peak uncertainty in August. No historical analog offered.

exchanges.question: What order trends are you seeing in large ag seasonal products and by region?
exchanges.answer: 2026 seasonal production set by closed EOPs. MY2027 sprayer EOP opened at the beginning of May and runs through the end of August in two phases; planters open beginning of June through end of September. Very early, don't extrapolate, but everything seen so far supports the view that 2026 marks the bottom of the ag cycle.

exchanges.question: Expected See & Spray acres this year, retrofit order trends, Precision Essentials renewal rates for the 2025 cohort, and list price increases for advanced EOP features.
exchanges.answer: See & Spray covered 1 million acres in year one and 5 million globally last year; same customers spraying more acres year-to-date; 50%-60% herbicide savings over two years; See & Spray Green on Green introduced in Brazil; 2027 take rates so far exceed this year. Seibert: Precision Essentials orders trending well, closer to 5,000 new Operations Center customer orgs. Beal: renewals in the 70% range overall, second-year renewal cohort over 90%; harvest settings automation utilization over 60% in Northern Hemisphere and over 80% in Brazil. No acreage target, retrofit figures or list price increases given.

exchanges.question: What is the Q3 and Q4 cadence for sales and margins, and could any region or segment deviate from normal seasonality?
exchanges.answer: Back half higher than front half, Q4 a little higher than Q3. Large ag Q4 stronger than Q3, abnormally, due to more Waterloo large tractor shipments to North America in the back half. Small Ag normal seasonality with step downs in Q3 and Q4. C&F fairly balanced, Q4 maybe a little stronger; nothing abnormal to call out.

exchanges.question: Do large ag pricing expectations, more conservative than peers, reflect higher discounting?
exchanges.answer: Price adjusted down quarter-over-quarter because of Brazil; all regions expected price positive in large ag; full-year 1% price guide, North America a bit better, other two regions a little lower. Seibert: second-half price better than first half as prior discounting is lapped; progress on used inventory and incentives positions pricing well.

exchanges.question: Is the ~$270 million IEEPA refund a true benefit versus the initial guide or offset by other tariffs returning exposure to $1.2 billion? And how can price-cost improve when raw materials, components and energy all point to tougher costs?
exchanges.answer: Beal: $1.2 billion tariff expense run rate unchanged with puts and takes; $272 million refund new in the quarter, netting to more like $900 million this year; agrees there have been high levels of inflation over the last two or three months, but back half laps last year's tariffs and indirect tariff inflation. Norwood: pricing much more favorable in the back half so price-cost ratios improve meaningfully; better overhead absorption in large ag factories in Q4 on significantly higher production rates.

exchanges.question: What sentiment and feedback are management and North American dealers hearing on large ag and how the spring EOP and 2027 capex might play out?
exchanges.answer: Beal: baseline is some recovery next year given fleet age and inventory work; John Deere Financial trade wholesale (used equipment financed on dealer lots) down over 15% YoY; about a third of old crop still to be sold, supported by higher commodity prices; more caution on next year's input costs. Norwood: dealer feedback varies; those who acted early on used are most optimistic, a couple even looking to add to used fleets; others more moderate.

exchanges.question: Are South American share gains coming from the existing product portfolio or driven by new product rollouts?
exchanges.answer: Share has risen steadily and fairly linearly over about a decade and a half in tractors and combines, from multiple fronts: new products and technologies, the dealer channel, localization; amplified by record product introductions (new combines, sprayers, planters, See & Spray, Starlink connectivity); harvest settings automation utilization highest globally in Brazil; extremely bullish on the region. No split given.
